weekly_intro.en: In the blink of an eye, the Fall 2026 anime season has flown past its opening stretch and is already approaching the halfway point. And yet, looking back at the season so far, it somehow doesn't feel that way at all. Is this season really going to be okay? Who am I kidding? Of course not. What on earth are we watching this season? What exactly are we being subjected to? I just can't shake those questions. Despite following over 30 anime, there's barely one show I could actually recommend this week. And now we've even got a series suddenly pulling out some absurd premise about being able to gain only one new follower every ten years—and shamelessly forcing it down our throats. Seriously, what the hell is going on? So, amid all this chaos, how did each series fare this week? Is there still any hope left for the season? Well, one way or another, let's take a look at the latest rankings!
weekly_intro.ja: 2026年秋アニメシーズンも、早いもので序盤も既に過ぎ、気づけばもう中盤の折り返し地点一歩手前の話数に差しかかろうとしています。本当にあっという間です。 とはいえ、ここまで振り返ってみても、そんな実感がまったく湧かないんですよね。ってそんなんで今期、大丈夫なんでしょうか？いや、ダメでしょう。今期、私たちは一体何を見ているのか、何を見せられているのか？そんな疑問を拭い去ることが出来ません。 さて、視聴作品だけで言えば３０作品超にも関わらず、おすすめ出来る作品が今週は１作品くらいしかありません、ましてや、“１０年に一人しか信者を増やすことが出来ない”なんてとんでも設定を唐突に持ち出し、ゴリ押す作品も出てくる始末…なんてことでしょう。 そんな混沌とした今週、各作品の評価はどうなのでしょうか？ 期待は保てるのでしょうか？ いずれにせよ、最新のランキングを見てみましょう！

reason.en:
Episode #4: The Boy Who Is the World's Strongest Sorcerer and His Friends Converse With Their Fists
"How could this series change so drastically? I thought the differences in animation were relatively minor, but their impact is surprisingly huge... What a crushing disappointment."

[I genuinely loved Season 1—I even rewatched it about twice—so seeing what this series has become is incredibly sad, disappointing, and frankly infuriating. This season is just too awful, so I'm saying goodbye to it as a ranking contender.

It's surprising how even seemingly subtle changes in the art and animation can completely alter the impression a show makes. But the bigger problem is the bizarre tone and the drastic shift toward exaggerated comedy and ridiculous antics. Now practically every female character seems hopelessly in love with the MC, and all we get is one scene after another of them fawning over him. This is NOT what the series used to be.

Even in this episode, the way the MC responds to Carol feels completely wrong. Didn't he firmly reject and push her away in Season 1? Seriously, I've had enough. I do intend to keep watching for now, but honestly, I'm not even sure about that anymore.]

Lent is part of the up-and-coming party known as the "Skypiercers," and thanks to his unique Gift, he can loan massive amounts of magic to others. No MP? No problem with Lent around! review.en:
Episode #5: Calamitous Monsters

"Everything about this show is a mystery. What the hell am I watching? Is it just supposed to be loud and obnoxious? Or is this secretly some otome-game-style, overpowered harem fantasy?"

What a baffling show. It's awful, obnoxiously loud, and downright irritating. The supposed Saintess just keeps flaunting how ridiculously powerful she is, using her past life as an excuse. The guys surrounding her were already pretty underwhelming, but this new guy who can supposedly sense monsters and magical power is even more unbearably noisy. I really don't think I can take much more of this.

And what's the deal with that girl who was declared a Saintess right at the beginning? What is she even supposed to be? Honestly, nothing about this show makes any sense.

"すべてが謎、ナニコレ?ただうるさいだけ?何気に乙女ゲー的なハーレム無双モノなの?"

source_entries.romanized_title: Tensei shita Daiseijo wa, Seijo de Aru Koto wo Hitakakusu
source_entries.synopsis:
Fia always dreamed of becoming a knight. Born into a family of knights, she's the least talented among them, but she still clutches to her hope and trains with everything she has. When the day comes for her to slay a small demon and prove her worth, she ends up face to face with a dragon instead! A deadly injury makes her life flash before her eyes... and she suddenly remembers her former life, when she was a powerful Saint in a bygone era who defeated the Demon King. That life ended in pain because of who she was, making her fear ever becoming a Saint again. Now that the magic from her previous life has been rekindled, she may become a more powerful knight than she ever dreamed–if only she can survive long enough!

(Source: Seven Seas Entertainment)
source_entries.synopsis_ja: 「剣の才能がない」と言われながらも騎士を目指す少女・フィーア。死にかけた彼女が思い出したのは、なんと規格外のチート能力を持つ「大聖女」としての前世で！？大聖女として騎士とともに戦い、最後に魔王の右腕によって無残に殺された300年前の過去だった――記憶を思い出したことで、「大聖女」の力も蘇ったフィーアだったが、前世で魔王の右腕から「聖女として生まれ変わったら殺す」と脅されたことを思い出し、その力を隠しながら騎士として生きていくことを決意する。しかし傷ついている人を見たら放っておけないフィーアは、度々遭遇する事件で頻繁に力を使ってしまう。果たして聖女であることをひた隠し続けることができるのか…！？

review.en:
Episode #4: How's the Weather Over There?

"A perfect portrayal of friendship, with every little detail beautifully woven into a railway journey. Absolutely wonderful! Seriously, what the hell was that first episode?"

Brilliant! I was genuinely moved. This episode focuses on Ushio and Kodama. The basic premise is simple: to celebrate Kodama's birthday, Ushio books a ride on the Watarase Keikoku Railway's scenic trolley train in Gunma Prefecture, somewhere Kodama has always wanted to visit.

Ushio is the kind of person who gets so caught up in trying her hardest that she overlooks important little details. She's determined to make Kodama happy, but naturally, she keeps making small mistakes along the way. Yet Kodama knows her longtime friend so well that she's already anticipated some of those slipups, even making a lunch reservation in advance. Her thoughtfulness shows up in little ways throughout the trip. Their friendship is beautifully portrayed through these moments as they enjoy the trolley train and explore the area together, despite a few mishaps along the way. It all comes together as a truly lovely birthday outing.

And choosing the Watarase Keikoku Railway as the setting? What a wonderful touch. I loved how the journey reflects what connects these two, and how Ushio and Kodama hope their two younger friends will remain just as close for years to come. There was also that curious reaction from Kodama when Ushio struck up a conversation with an older man selling boxed lunches on the platform at an intermediate station. I wondered what that was about, and the eventual payoff during their meal in that charming restaurant housed in an old railway carriage was absolutely delightful. The way it all came together through their conversation was just perfect.

I also continue to enjoy Arisa's appearances on the Matsuura Railway in each episode's post-credits segment. This time, the older woman's closing remark—roughly, "If only everyone could see the look on your face right now, Arisa!"—was especially sharp and funny.

Absolutely no complaints. I'm almost certainly sticking with this one until the end. It's rapidly becoming one of my favorite anime of the season.
review.jp:
第4話: そちらの天気はどうですか?

"完璧な、2人の友情、そのあり方が鉄道の旅に散りばめられ最高、あの第1話はなんだったんだ?"

素晴らしい!感動した。今回スポットがあたった2人はうしおとこだま。

あらすじは、ざっと、— こだまの誕生日を祝うため、うしおは彼女がずっと行ってみたいと話していた群馬県のわたらせ渓谷鐵道・トロッコ列車の予約を取る—ということになっている。 何かに一生懸命になると、肝心なことを忘れてしまったりする、うしおがこだまに喜んでもらおうと、奔走するが、やはり小さなミスを連発してしまう。それでも長いこと仲良しでいる2人なだけあり、こだまはうしおのおっちょこちょいを予測してお弁当の予約を入れておいたり、そこかしこに気遣いも見せる。そんな2人のあり方が、色々とありつつも2人でトロッコ列車や沿線の旅を満喫し、素敵な誕生日のお出かけ回となる、という今回の話の至るところに散りばめられていた。

またその旅先がわたらせ渓谷鐵道というのもオツ過ぎる。二人をつなぐもの、そしてそんなうしおとこだまが後輩の2人にも自分たちの様にずっと仲良くいて欲しいと願うなんて・・・素晴らしかった。うしおが途中の駅で駅弁の手売りをしているオジサンに話しかけている時のこだまの妙な反応が気になったが、それが後で種明かしされた時の素敵な古い車両レストランでの食事シーンでの会話につながるの最高だった。

そして毎回Cパートに登場する松浦鉄道のありさもいい。今回のおばさんの返しである「今のありさちゃんの顔もみんなに見てもらえばよかっちゃなぁ」の〆もキレがあって良かった。申し分無し。これは最期まで見るでしょう。今期かなり好きな作品に急上昇です。

review.en:
Episode #3: (Total #16): Tomorrow's Wind

"I have so many mixed feelings about this episode, but in the end... it was unmistakably feel. It was Summer Pockets all over again. If only they'd cut back on the endless poetry..."

I suppose it all depends on how you choose to take it. But one thing's certain: this was feel. through and through... and it was Summer Pockets all over again. Once again, I found myself dragged into that familiar world where apparently anything goes as long as you turn it into some fairy-tale-like, dreamlike seven days of summer. Do they seriously think they can get away with absolutely anything that way?

And yet, even while thinking, "Oh, come on..." I found myself enjoying it. That's feel. for you, I guess. Of course, everything is ridiculously overdone, and the relentless poetic monologues become so excessive that they're practically noise. I kept wishing they'd at least tone that down, but then again, maybe that's precisely what makes this series what it is. The whole thing is so relentlessly poetic that I end up going back and forth in my own head, almost as if I've fallen into the same kind of emotional trap myself.

The imagery of "the moon and the marble inside a ramune bottle" also seems absolutely central to this series, something it simply refuses to compromise on. It comes up repeatedly, but it really is memorable, and I thought the way it ultimately came to represent the relationship between these two was genuinely beautiful.

A few things bothered me, though. With so much packed into a single episode, the second half in particular felt rather rushed. Asu-nee's father's sudden change in attitude also seemed a little too easy, but I can let that slide. After all, considering the kind of person he is, I suppose it makes sense that he's been friends with that ridiculous homeroom teacher for so many years.

What I particularly loved this time was seeing Asu-nee become that cool, wonderful Asu-nee everyone back home knows and admires once again. At the same time, there was something deeply touching about how she came to realize that the future she hoped for would probably never arrive. Despite her loneliness, she chose to accept that reality and move forward. And it was precisely that acceptance that led her to the decision to "leave everything here, in this moment." I thought that was beautiful.

And Chitose Saku... Seriously, what an unbelievably irresponsible guy! He has the charm and potential to end up with practically every girl around him—and frankly, he acts as though he's deliberately keeping every possibility open—yet he doesn't actually choose anyone? What the hell is that supposed to be?!

At some point, I even caught myself thinking, "Oh, just pick Asu-nee already! She seems like she'd be a handful, but whatever!" Maybe that's a pretty creepy thought on my part? Or maybe the fact that I found myself thinking something so ridiculous is proof that I actually enjoyed this episode quite a lot. That's how I'm choosing to look at it, anyway.
review.jp:
第3話: (通算16話): 明日の風

"色々思うところはありまくりながらもやはり…feel.だった…サマポケだった…あとは、ポエムさえ無ければ…"

これはどう受け止めるか次第だろう。とにかく、feel.だった…、そしてサマーポケッツだった。お得意の何でもその御伽の国の夏の日の幻の7日間にしてしまえば、何でも通用すると思ってるのか?という世界に連れ込まれてしまった。

おいおい…と思いつつも楽しんでいる自分もいたりしながら、やっぱこれぞfeel.だよなぁ~と思ってみたり。もちろん色んな意味でやり過ぎだし、とにかくポエム過ぎてノイズにもなっている。だらか、せめてそれが無ければとも思うが、それも本作の本作たる所以かとも思ったり。どこまで行ってもポエムなので、こちらも行ったり来たりの思考のトラップにでもハマったみたいになる。

また、"月とラムネ瓶の中のビー玉"という表現は、本作にとって、主題でもあり、決して譲れないものなのだろう。それも繰り返し出てくるが、印象的だし、この2人の関係性において最終的にとても素敵なものとして印象に残る描かれ方がされていたと思う。

他に気になった点と言えば、1話に詰め込んでいるので、特に後半早足にも感じたり、アスカ姉(ネエ)の父親態度があまりにもあっさりと切り替わるのもちょっと…とも感じたけど、まぁいいかと思える範囲。そんな人間だからこそ、このふざけた担任とも長年仲良くしているのだろうし。

個人的に今回良かったと思えたのは、アスカ姉(ネエ)がやはり地元でかっこいい素敵な明日姉に戻ったことかな。そしてそれとは対照的に、きっと来くることがない未来を悟って淋しくなりながらも、それを受け止め歩む決心をしたこと、だからこそ「今ここに全部を置いていく」という在り方に辿り着いたことだろう。

千歳朔、本当に全く持って無責任な奴よ。全員とくっつける素養、可能性、いやそれを想定した行動を取っていながら、誰ともくっつかないってさ、なんなの?ですよ。自分としてはどこかで、「いいじゃんアスカ姉(ネエ)にしときなよ、面倒くそうだけど」、とどうでもいい気持ちになったりで（キモいか?）、でもそれはつまり、今回の話を十分に楽しんだんだという証拠なのかな?とも受け取っております。

review.en:
Episode #5: Looking For A Repair Shop

"Another episode exploring everyone's feelings, struggles, efforts, and growth. I also loved Touka the repairer's story. What a lovely sound."

Another good episode. Apparently, there are still people scattered around outside the group's home base, even though we hardly ever see anyone. It's a little convenient how they only seem to run into people when the story needs them to, but I guess that's just part of the deal with zombie stories.

This time, I really liked everything: Natsuki struggling to adapt to life after losing an arm, Aki mysteriously hunting deer like crazy, Yuu's emotional growth, and the feelings and motivations behind Touka's work as a repairer. I especially liked the revelation that Aki had actually been looking for goats because she wanted to make pudding for Natsuki to celebrate what happened last time.

The characters' individual personalities, struggles, and growth are all portrayed with real care. With so many absolute garbage shows crowding this season, this series is doing remarkably well by comparison. I'm looking forward to more. Next stop: Tokyo Tower!

review.en:
Episode #5: (Total #19): Transition / Vicissitudes

"Each person's changes are like separate dots, sometimes connecting into lines as their lives intersect. In the end, it all comes down to what you choose to do, rather than endlessly thinking things through... I'm starting to tire of this obsession with analysis and introspection."

This episode shifts the focus away from Koyun and Yota, whose feelings for each other have dominated the story for a while, and instead explores Miki, Minato, and Momoka. Through their self-reflection, we see how they come to understand themselves and perceive the people around them. In other words, it's another episode of extraordinarily insightful psychological analysis and character portrayal. I'm honestly getting pretty tired of it by now, but I still can't help thinking, "Man, this is really well done. It's impressive."

The problem is that this kind of brilliance doesn't necessarily translate into emotional appeal. It may be what makes the series remarkable, but it doesn't automatically make the characters more likable or make me eager to keep watching. In fact, because the show explores everyone's individual circumstances and feelings so thoroughly, you eventually realize that everyone has their own story, making it difficult to blame anyone. Worse, I even find myself understanding and sympathizing with characters I previously thought were absolutely awful. Damn this show!

I did enjoy the contrast between Koyun, who seems to have sorted everything out in her own head without even consulting Miki and is acting perfectly fine, and Miki, who's left feeling shocked and hurt. Ultimately, though, the question is how much longer I can put up with all this overthinking and overanalyzing, and whether the series can maintain the balance between psychological depth and actual entertainment that it's managed so far.

I'm getting tired of watching everyone make their lives so unnecessarily complicated. I just want to tell them, "What's the point of thinking everything to death? People don't even fully understand themselves, let alone anyone else!"
review.jp:
第5話: (通算第19話) : 変遷

"個々の変遷は点と点、時には線で交わる世界線の共有、いずれにしても自分がどうするか次第、考えるより…。ちょっと分析?思考への偏重に飽きが…。"

暫くの間ずっと話題の焦点だった、"想い人"である陽太とコユンの2人以外の美姫、湊、桃香の自己観察から見えてくる気づき、相手、対象の姿のようなものが描かれた今回、要するにいつも通りの分析力が半端ない心理、人物描写でした。流石にもうお腹いっぱいではあるんだけど、"うまいよなぁ~、凄いなぁ"と素直に思える作品であることには変わりない。ただやっぱり、そういうものなだけに魅力にはつながりにくい。作品の魅力ではあっても、キャラの魅力や視聴意欲に直接結びつきにくいし、特に本作は、個々の事情や心理を描くので、結局それぞれにそれぞれのドラマがあり、そこを丹念に描くと、誰も責められないと言うか、以前は「このキャラ最悪」と思った対象にすら理解し、多少の感情移入をし出す始末。タチが悪い。美姫に相談もせず自己完結してサバサバしている（様に見える）コユンとショックを受ける美姫とか面白かった。いずれにしても"理屈コネ過ぎ"にどこまでついていけるか、そしてこれまではうまく行っている"面白さとの兼ね合い"もどこまで保てるか・・・だろう。もうこじらせるの面倒い・・・。「考えてもしょうがないでしょうよ・・・。人は自分のことも、ましてや他人のことなど分かりはしないのだから。」と言いたい。

Episode #5: (Total #53) : The White-Snake Immortal

"Quite an elaborate setup for a cheap little shock show. But in the end, it was really just another Maomao-explains-everything show. And Jinshi? We don't need him."

I enjoyed this episode, and personally, I'm fine with what it delivered. This series tends to spend a considerable number of episodes building toward developments in the latter half, so apart from a few standout episodes early or midway through, much of it inevitably feels like a work in progress. Still, the way it keeps things entertaining through little interactions, mysteries, and revelations while steadily laying the groundwork is genuinely impressive.

That said, the albino woman wasn't particularly compelling this time. She barely felt mysterious at all, and although I couldn't figure out the exact trick, something about it already seemed rather underwhelming. In the end, it was basically another Maomao explanation show, leaving me thinking, "Yeah, yeah, you're amazing. We get it." That feeling was stronger than usual this time. Having her figure out even the tiniest details also felt a bit excessive.

And for some reason... Jinshi is here again. Seriously, I'd be perfectly happy if he only showed up once in a while. Anyway, I'm being a little more reserved with my rating this time, but the series still maintains such a high standard that it's an 8.

Episode #5

Episode #5ː eitokai Gasshuku!! / Ume Tan-Tan Daisakusen!! / Kasa de Kasanaru Ame no Um
"Still as outrageous as ever! It's entertaining, no doubt, but can the show really keep this up forever?"

[The hot spring trip (?) in Part A, the shared umbrella, Terui's weakness... all of it was entertaining. The hot spring was riddled with peepholes, yet the characters insist that "nothing actually happened"—meanwhile, the audience got quite an eyeful of the girls anyway. I also loved how the student council president and Ume-kun somehow ended up sleeping together, and the fact that everyone got completely soaked in the rain was hilarious, too. (Not to mention the research club president casually letting something slip without making a big deal of it...)

That said, unless the series offers a little more beyond its outrageous antics and all the naughty stuff, I can see myself eventually getting bored—or simply getting so used to it all that my reaction becomes, "Yep, just another typical episode." I really hope it doesn't quietly settle into being a regular fixture in the 8-point range, or even the high 7s.

The sheer amount of material they pack into each episode is impressive, and the creators' enthusiasm is practically overflowing. That's why I'm hoping there's more to come.]

review.en:
Episode #4

Episode $4 (Total #29): Love Is The Most Powerful Feeling
"I'm still fed up with all the convenient contrivances, but this episode did have meaningful developments and some genuinely well-handled moments..."

[Ultimately, my reaction is simply, "It's not bad, but..." Everyone in this show is a good person deep down. Even those who seem prickly, mean, or downright unpleasant—especially the athletes—turn out to have their own struggles and reasons for acting that way, often hiding behind a tough exterior to protect themselves. And then these bright, shining people like Taiki and Chinatsu, who have their own struggles too, somehow come along and help them realize what's really going on. The show seems almost obsessed with turning everything into a beautiful, emotionally moving story. And frankly, I often find it rather sickening.

I think the biggest problem is how the story conveniently pulls out whatever it needs, whenever it needs it, just to create those emotional moments. Yumeka's boyfriend is absurdly perceptive and unbelievably mature. Then there's the Christmas date scheduled for the exact same time as Chinatsu's game, and the ticket conveniently placed right on top of a clear folder on the table, practically screaming, "Go ahead, take a look while I'm away!" Taiki and Chinatsu also keep running into each other at precisely the right moments—unless the plot needs them not to, of course. These coincidences just keep piling up until I want to scream, "Enough already! Stop shoving these emotional moments down my throat!"

Still, this episode had several genuinely worthwhile elements, the storytelling was fairly cohesive, and I can see how Yumeka's arc serves a meaningful purpose. So despite all my complaints, I think it deserves an 8.]
review.jp:
第4話: (第29話): 好きは最強の感情

"相変わらずのご都合ぶりには呆れるが、意味のある内容と展開、いい描き方もあったと思う・・・"

悪くないんだけど・・・、に尽きる。みんないい人。一見とんがってたり、意地悪そうだったり、根性曲がってそうだったりしても、みんな(特にスポーツマンは)何かしらの事情や想いがあって表面上そう見えたり、自分を守るために殻を被ったりしている。でもタイキや千夏や他の連中みたいにキラキラ輝いてる奴らが自らも苦しんだりしながら、それに気付いたり気づかせてくれる・・・そういった美しい話を感動的に描くことに偏りすぎている気がする。それが個人的には"気持ち悪い"と感じる時も多々ある。それはきっと描きたいものに必要なものを必要なときだけ都合よく使うスタイルが主な理由だろう。夢佳の彼氏の異常な気付きと人間の出来ているっぷり、そしてクリスマスの約束の時間がチ千夏の試合開始と全く同じ時間、またそのチケットを「さぁ、席を外している間に見てください」と言わんばかりにクリアファイルの一番上に挟んでテーブルの上に置いている・・・とか、タイキと千夏もいつもタイミングよく出くわすし（タイミンが悪いと出くわさない）、まぁもういい加減にしてくれ!ってくらいそういうことが重なりまくって、「"感動の押し売り"は止めてくれ!」と言いたくなる。まぁ、それでも今回は評価に値すると思える点もいくつかあったし、全体的にもまとまってたし、夢佳アークが意味を持つ感じなのも理解出来るので８点の評価。

review.en:
Episode #5: When we go home

"This one's heavily dependent on your mood, personal taste, and the atmosphere you're in when watching. I liked the Princess, the Cold One, and the Squirrel, but..."

Personally, I like this series, but I suspect how much you enjoy it depends heavily on your mood and what you're in the mood to watch. The key is probably what the show chooses to present, what it wants viewers to notice or become curious about, and whether it actually succeeds in making them care. Even for someone like me, who genuinely likes its atmosphere, it's becoming a bit of a mixed bag.

Whatever happened to the Princess and the Cold One? Are we just focusing on the Not-Sleepy One and Eleonora now? Hmm... I'm not particularly interested, to be honest. I suspect these threads will eventually connect in interesting ways, but I'm starting to wonder whether there's much point in keeping this series in my rankings.

Episode #4: A New Daily Life

"So far, it's making steady progress and remains reasonably entertaining... but I'm starting to want a little more variety in pacing, drama, and a clearer sense of direction."

It's a fairly ordinary episode, but for now, I'm taking that as a sign of steady, solid progress. With Elma joining Mimi—another addition to the harem, though he hasn't actually married either of them—the three settle into their new life together, enjoying their little harem arrangement while gradually moving toward the next developments. I thought the episode handled that progression reasonably well. Is he going to add that high-ranking military officer to his harem too?

Still, I can't help thinking this show could earn a higher score if it did a better job of showcasing just how skilled and capable the MC really is.

review.en:
Episode #16

Episode #5ː The Line Between Courage and Recklessness
"It looks promising at first glance, but questionable details are scattered everywhere... I'm starting to suspect this series will end up being a disappointment."

[Beyond its premise, this series doesn't have much going for it. This episode's battle against the demons seemed pretty good on the surface, but the more I thought about it, the less convincing it became. Last time, everyone was in serious trouble, yet this episode somehow starts after they've apparently escaped that predicament. How? And why are they suddenly able to fend off the demons?

Then there's Al, who was supposedly so badly injured he couldn't even move on his own, yet somehow fights the enemy squad leader like he's perfectly fine. Both Ray and Al also conveniently awaken magical abilities they apparently had all along, allowing them to land effective attacks. Even the other soldiers suddenly manage to defeat the ordinary demons they struggled so desperately against last time.

We also get a strangely placed flashback to Romelia's past, showing her happily spending time with the prince—wait, they actually had a loving relationship?! Then Romelia gets injured by the enemy squad leader, which feels like yet another conveniently manufactured crisis. And when he tries to attack her again at the end, something suddenly bursts into flames... What was that? Was it Ray? Al? Who caused it, and when? I honestly couldn't figure it out, even after watching the scene twice.

I do appreciate the growing bond between Romelia and her troops, the attempts at strategy, and the effort put into certain aspects of the episode. But overall, I'm starting to think this series isn't nearly as good as I'd hoped.]

"一見良さそうに見えて微妙な点がそこかしこに散らばる・・・期待外れに終わりそうな予感"

設定意外に魅力が乏しい。今回の魔族との闘いは良さそうに見えて、実はそうでもなかった。前回かなり追い詰められていたのに、今回始まったらその難は何とか切り抜けた（らしい?）後から始まるし、何気に魔族を振り払えてるのも何故か分からない。そして重症を負って自分だけで動けない筈のアルが敵の小隊長との戦闘ではバリバリ動ける、そしてレイもアルも謎に潜在能力だけはあった魔法が発現?して有効打が出せるようになる。他の兵士たちも、前回あれだけ苦戦していた雑兵の魔族をやっつける。冒頭のロメリアの過去、王子と仲睦まじかった時（そんなのあったんかい!）の回想を謎に差し込んだり、ロメリアも小隊長にやられて負傷したり・・・。それもピンチのご都合にしか見えない。また最期に敵の小隊長がロメリアに襲いかかろうとした時に謎の発火・・・いつの?レイ?アル?がやったの?よくわかんなかったなぁ・・・2回見たけど・・・。ロメリアとその率いる舞台のいい感じの結束の強まりとか、ある程度の戦略とか、まぁ頑張ってた所は評価するけど、思ったほどの作品じゃない気がする。

review.en:
Episode #5: So What's Wrong With Being Disliked By An Adlescent Elf?

"Just another goblin village chief surrounded by a harem. No, I don't have any questions. I'm not interested... Did you seriously think I would?"

This episode was pretty awful, honestly. Sloppy, more than anything. It basically consisted of Akira, our goblin village chief, being ridiculously popular with the elves and getting constantly hit on by gorgeous, busty, sexy women. Everything else felt like an afterthought, and none of it was particularly entertaining.

I also wasn't impressed by the use of obvious Japanese-derived names like Echigoya to make characters' roles immediately recognizable, including the guy who makes clothes. Then there's the whole business of tattooing the foreheads of people trying to sneak into the village, with ridiculous messages like "I lost to a goblin." That joke completely fell flat. And if these intruders keep coming back, why not just use his Survival of the Fittest ability on them from the start?

Anyway, the bottom line is that it was simply boring. I'm being a little generous with a 7 this time, but if the next episode is more of the same, it's dropping to a 6.
review.jp:
第5話: 思春期エルフに嫌われてるんだけど質問ある?

"ただのハーレムゴブリン村長でしたが、質問などありません、興味ないですから・・・あると思ってるの?"

今回は結構酷かったな・・・雑というか。とにかくエルフを初めアキラ（MCゴブリン村長）がモテまくる、そして美女巨乳ホットな連中に迫られアピールされまくるだけ・・・って感じ。その他の要素はオマケ程度にしか感じないし面白くもなかった。越後屋とか何だか日本語由来のわかりやすい名前で役柄を明確にする（洋服を作る奴とか）ってのもなんだかいい印象を持てない。村に侵入しようとしてくる連中の額に入れ墨をするってのも、その「私はゴブリンに負けました」みたいな文言も滑ってるし・・・。しつこい侵入者にはもう最初から弱肉強食使えばいいじゃんって話だし。まぁとにかく"つまらなかった"。今回はちょっと緩めに7点だが次回からもこうなら6点にする。

entries.synopsis:
Three high school girls—hot-blooded Hikaru Shidou, haughty Umi Ryuuzaki, and gentle Fuu Hououji—have just met at Tokyo Tower when they hear a call for help that pulls them into another world. They are soon greeted by Guru Clef, a youthful-looking man who informs them that they are the legendary Magic Knights summoned by Princess Emeraude to save this magical land known as Cephiro.

While Hikaru finds the prospect exciting, Umi and Fuu simply want to return to their own world. Unfortunately for them, Clef explains that they cannot go home until they have saved Cephiro and banished the monsters plaguing it. In order to do so, they have to rescue Princess Emeraude from the clutches of the powerful Lord Zagato. To stand a chance against him, they must revive mysterious beings called Rune Gods.

As Clef grants the trio armor and magic, one of Zagato's servants attacks, forcing the guru to send the girls away to the weaponsmith Presea and the rabbit-like guide Mokona, who can further equip them for their journey. Though they have a long way to go, Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu will show that they have what it takes to live up to their titles as Magic Knights and bring salvation to Cephiro.

[Written by MAL Rewrite]
